item.title: Heterogeneous cycling of molybdenum and other trace metals in oxic to suboxic Pacific pelagic sediments
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 28 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04210-7

Different redox conditions and Mn-oxide mineral phases drive contrasting trace-metal cycling, particularly for molybdenum, in sediments underlying polymetallic nodule areas, according to analysis of trace metal heterogeneity of two exploration contract areas for polymetallic nodule mining in the Pacific.
item.dc:title: Heterogeneous cycling of molybdenum and other trace metals in oxic to suboxic Pacific pelagic sediments

item.title: Storyline attribution of fire weather during the 2025 Mediterranean summer
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04238-9

Climate change substantially intensified fire-conducive weather across the Mediterranean in the summer of 2025, primarily through higher temperatures, based on a spectrally nudged storyline attribution framework.
item.dc:title: Storyline attribution of fire weather during the 2025 Mediterranean summer

item.title: Microplastic polymer hazard is associated with soil microbial community structure and functionality
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04237-w

Polymer-specific hazard, not microplastic load, governs how microbial communities are restructured under microplastics pollution stress in China’s black soil region, according to a combination of bulk soil surveys in 50 farms with stress-gradient incubation experiments.
item.dc:title: Microplastic polymer hazard is associated with soil microbial community structure and functionality

item.title: Anthropogenic impacts shift carbon dioxide emissions from Chinese rivers from historical reductions to future increases
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04219-y

Riverine CO2 emissions from Chinese rivers declined historically but are projected to rise by 17% by 2100 due to longer ice-free seasons, expanding river areas and increasing emission density, suggests a study using explainable machine learning to reconstruct and project emissions from 1980 to 2100.
item.dc:title: Anthropogenic impacts shift carbon dioxide emissions from Chinese rivers from historical reductions to future increases

item.title: Global assessment of solar encroachment on cropland and food production
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04221-4

Global photovoltaic expansion on cropland threatens food production, with losses projected to increase 12–22-fold by 2050, though mitigation measures could substantially reduce impacts, according to global photovoltaic mapping, crop-production estimation and future scenario modeling.
item.dc:title: Global assessment of solar encroachment on cropland and food production

item.title: Typhoon intensity forecasting using deep learning and physics-guided SHIPS-based predictors
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04229-w

An attention-based deep learning framework with spatially varying physical predictors outperforms operational forecasts for tropical cyclone intensity at 24–48-hour lead times, reducing 24-hour mean absolute error and capturing thermodynamic mechanisms of intensity change.
item.dc:title: Typhoon intensity forecasting using deep learning and physics-guided SHIPS-based predictors
